commands.name: rstory
commands.help:
A small, private clipboard history for Linux

Usage: rstory [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  daemon                   Run the clipboard daemon in the foreground
  ls                       List the history, newest first
  show                     Print an entry's content, byte for byte
  copy                     Put an entry back on the clipboard
  pin                      Pin an entry so it survives clearing and expiry
  unpin                    Unpin an entry
  rm                       Delete one entry
  clear                    Delete the unpinned entries (all of them with --all)
  pause                    Stop recording, for a while or until `resume`
  resume                   Start recording again
  status                   Show the daemon state and counters
  config                   Show the effective configuration
  pick                     Open the interactive picker
  doctor                   Check the setup and explain what is wrong
  tray                     Show the tray icon from a separate process (for `tray = false`)
  install-autostart        Start the daemon at login
  install-gnome-extension  Install the GNOME Shell extension
  completions              Print a shell completion script
  help                     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --ascii
          Use only ASCII glyphs (also the default in a non-UTF-8 locale)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Entries are addressed by index (0 is the newest) or by a short id of at least 4 characters.

Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 unexpected, 2 usage or not found, 3 daemon not running, 4 daemon already running, 5 environment error, 6 limit reached, 7 inactive.

commands.name: daemon
commands.help:
Run the clipboard daemon in the foreground.

Usage: rstory daemon [--backend x11|wayland]

  --backend x11|wayland  capture with this backend instead of the one the session selects
                         (also --backend=x11); wins over `backend` in config.toml
  -h, --help             print this help

The daemon records what you copy, serves `rstory` and the tray over a private socket, and
logs to stderr (RUST_LOG, default info). Exit codes: 0 clean stop, 4 already running,
5 environment error, 1 unexpected.

Examples:
  rstory daemon
  rstory daemon --backend x11
  RUST_LOG=debug rstory daemon

commands.name: ls
commands.help:
List the history, newest first

Usage: rstory ls [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --ascii
          Use only ASCII glyphs (also the default in a non-UTF-8 locale)

      --json
          Print JSON (`schema` 1) instead of lines

      --limit <N>
          Show at most N entries

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Examples:
  rstory ls
  rstory ls --limit 5
  rstory ls --json | jq '.entries[].short_id'

commands.name: show
commands.help:
Print an entry's content, byte for byte

Usage: rstory show [OPTIONS] <REF>

Arguments:
  <REF>
          Index (0 = newest) or short id (4+ characters)

Options:
      --ascii
          Use only ASCII glyphs (also the default in a non-UTF-8 locale)

      --json
          Print JSON (`schema` 1) instead of the raw content

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Examples:
  rstory show 0
  rstory show 01JB | wc -c
  rstory show 1 --json

      --ascii

commands.name: pause
commands.help:
Stop recording, for a while or until `resume`

Usage: rstory pause [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --ascii
          Use only ASCII glyphs (also the default in a non-UTF-8 locale)

      --for <DURATION>
          How long: 50s, 2m or 1h (1s to 24h)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Examples:
  rstory pause
  rstory pause --for 50s
  rstory pause --for 2m && pass -c mysite

commands.name: pick
commands.help:
Open the interactive picker

Usage: rstory pick [--plain] [--ascii]

commands.name: doctor
commands.help:
Check the setup and explain what is wrong. Read-only: it changes nothing.

Usage: rstory doctor [--json] [--ascii]

  --json   print the report as JSON
  --ascii  use only ASCII glyphs

Exit codes: 0 everything works, 1 warnings, 2 failures (or a usage error).

Examples:
  rstory doctor
  rstory doctor --json | jq '.checks[] | select(.status != "ok")'

commands.name: install-autostart
commands.help:
Start the rstory daemon at login.

Usage: rstory install-autostart [--systemd] [--now] [--uninstall]

  --systemd    write a systemd user unit instead of an XDG autostart entry
  --now        also start the daemon now
  --uninstall  remove both kinds

Examples:
  rstory install-autostart
  rstory install-autostart --systemd --now

commands.name: install-gnome-extension
commands.help:
Install the rstory GNOME Shell extension (Shell 48 to 50) from this binary.

Usage: rstory install-gnome-extension [--enable | --uninstall]

  --enable     also run `gnome-extensions enable` (works after a re-login)
  --uninstall  remove the extension

Examples:
  rstory install-gnome-extension
  rstory install-gnome-extension --uninstall

commands.name: completions
commands.help:
Print a shell completion script

Usage: rstory completions [OPTIONS] <SHELL>

Arguments:
  <SHELL>
          The shell

          Possible values:
          - bash: bash
          - zsh:  zsh
          - fish: fish

Options:
      --ascii
          Use only ASCII glyphs (also the default in a non-UTF-8 locale)

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

  -V, --version
          Print version

Examples:
  rstory completions bash > ~/.local/share/bash-completion/completions/rstory
  rstory completions fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/rstory.fish
